The page says the Philistines 'settled in Canaan around 1175 BC' and that in the first stage, 'dated to the reign of Ramesses III, they were limited to the coastal plain, the region of the Five Cities'; the shape is wider than the five cities, so the northern part is the later stage the page's extract does not date (unverified: page budget). No area on any page. Fix 2026-10-19: the Gaza district (10 cells) is held by Egypt until c. 1136 (Ramesses VI page: 'the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine around the time'), so it joins in the -1136 gain and the full shape stands from -1136 (next keyframe). The Gibeah cell (Saul's capital, kingdom-of-israel) is also cut. The first stage was 'limited to the coastal plain, the region of the Five Cities'; the pentapolis is Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath. [Fix 2026-10-19: the Gaza district (10 of the 38 cells, the 40 km circle that new-kingdom-of-egypt /ledger/22 gives up in -1136) is left out until the -1136 gain, so that the two dossiers do not draw it twice. The Philistines page does not say Gaza was Egyptian; it has Ramesses III settle the pwrꜣsꜣtj 'in strongholds, bound in my name' (Harris Papyrus) and speaks of 'the collapse of Egyptian hegemony in southern Canaan' without a year, so the Egyptian hold is the Egyptian dossier's reading of the Ramesses VI page.] [Fix 2026-10-19: the Gibeah district (1 cell, 35.21 E 31.87 N, inside Cliopatria's shape) is left out because kingdom-of-israel holds it from -1047 as Saul's capital.]

ledger.note: c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Philistia becomes a client of David's Israel. The united-monarchy page has David expand his sphere to 'control the weaker client states of Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon' and defeat 'the Philistines to secure his borders', as the biblical account and with no year (David 'rules from c. 1000 to 961 BCE'). Philistia is the vassal and kingdom-of-israel the suzerain; mirrors kingdom-of-israel /ledger/2 (reviewer fix).

ledger.note: c. 1000 BCE (bridged): the southern end of the inland strip leaves Philistia without passing to Israel. Cliopatria's 1000 shape no longer has this cell and no neighbour's does; page silent.

c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends when the united monarchy divides. The page puts the division 'in about 930 BCE' ('Jeroboam's Revolt: 930 BCE'); it does not say what became of the client states; mirrors kingdom-of-israel /ledger/9.

ledger.note: c. 900 BCE (bridged): the northern Philistine coast passes to Israel. Cliopatria's shape cut; the Philistia page names no such change and no year.

ledger.note: c. 900 BCE (bridged): the southern coastal fringe leaves Philistia. Cliopatria's shape cut; no state in the neighbour list holds it, and the page is silent.

c. 830 BCE: Hazael of Aram-Damascus destroys Gath. The Tell es-Safi page cites 2010 reports of 'evidence of destruction by King Hazael of Aram-Damascus around 830 BCE'; Gath was 'A large city in the Iron Age'. A one-year contest: Gath was captured again in 711.
c. 830 BCE (bridged): the raid ends in the same year; no occupation is recorded and Gath remained a Philistine city until 711.

734 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III's fifth Levant campaign reaches the Egyptian border. The Tiglath-Pileser III page: in 734 he conquered Gaza, and Ashkelon, Judah, Edom, Moab, Ammon and the Mu'na tribe began paying tribute. The Philistia page says he occupied Philistia in the 8th century BC and the Philistines page that he 'marched into the region'. The year is the page's; applying it to all Five Cities is the researcher's reading, and the cities keep their kings as tributaries (Sennacherib took tribute from Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron in 701), so the land is occupied, not annexed.

711 BC: Sargon II captures Gath. 'In his annals concerning the campaign, Sargon II singled out his capture of Gath, in 711 BC'; Ashdod had a new king, Iamani, 'in 712 BC'. Gath is not heard of again (Tell es-Safi: destroyed 'by the Assyrians in the late eighth century BCE').

region.text: the plundered lands of Judah on the Philistine frontier, given to Ashdod, Gaza and Ekron

ledger.note: 701 BC: Sennacherib gives Judah's plundered lands to the Philistine kings. The Philistia page says he divided Judah's plundered lands among the kings of Ashdod, Gaza and Ekron on his third Levantine campaign (no year; the Philistines page has 'Ten years later' than 711, so 701). The band along the Judah frontier is the researcher's reading of 'Judah's lands'.
609 BC: Egypt replaces Assyria. 'The Philistines were later occupied by the Egyptians in 609 BC, under Necho II.'
609 BC: Necho II occupies the Philistine cities ('occupied by the Egyptians in 609 BC, under Necho II').
604 BC: the Egyptian occupation ends when Babylon invades.

604 BC: Nebuchadnezzar II annexes Philistia. The Philistia page has Nebuchadnezzar II's forces invading Philistia in 604 BC, annexing it and destroying Ashkelon and Ekron after revolts (its era line gives the Babylonian conquest of the Levant as 604 BC); the Philistines page adds Gaza and Aphek to the destroyed cities.

604 BC: Philistia ends. Philistia and its people then disappear from recorded history until the 2nd century BC (Philistia page); the Philistines 'no longer appear as a distinct group' by the late 5th century.

wars.name: Israelite-Philistine wars

zones.text: the inland strip lost to Israel

wars.outcome: The Philistines defeat the Israelites at Aphek and Gilboa (killing Saul) and are beaten at Eben-ezer and the Valley of Elah; David then makes Philistia a client state.
wars.note: No year on the Philistines page for any battle; the span is the united-monarchy reigns (Saul 1047–1010, David 1008–970).

wars.name: Hazael's destruction of Gath
wars.outcome: Gath destroyed c. 830 BCE; the city survived to 711.
wars.note: The date rests on 'evidence of destruction' in 2010 excavation reports.

wars.name: Sargon II's campaign against Ashdod and Gath
wars.outcome: Assyria installs and removes rulers at Ashdod and captures Gath in 711.
wars.note: The Philistia page says Egypt often incited Philistine revolts against Assyria in the 8th century BC.

wars.name: Sennacherib's third campaign in the Levant

zones.text: Judah's lands on the Philistine frontier

wars.outcome: Tribute from Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron; Judah's plundered lands divided among the kings of Ashdod, Gaza and Ekron; Jaffa reassigned to Sidon.
wars.note: The Philistia page does not date the campaign; 701 is computed from the Philistines page ('Ten years later' than 711).

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar II's conquest of Philistia
wars.outcome: Philistia annexed; Ashkelon and Ekron destroyed (Gaza and Aphek too on the Philistines page).

certainty.note: The Five Cities' territories were never surveyed; every edge, especially the inland and Judah frontiers, is approximate.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: 'Philistia' -1150..-701, 5 shapes (10,865; 7,635; 3,137; 3,291; 3,291 km2). The row ends 97 years before the Babylonian annexation of 604; the dossier extends the 750 shape to -604 as a tributary confederation (new keyframes -711 and -701) and records Assyrian (-734), Egyptian (609) and Babylonian (604) control as occupations, not annexations, because the pages have Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron paying tribute and keeping kings in 701. CONFLICT WITH THE NEO-ASSYRIAN DOSSIER: that dossier records a gain from philistia at -734 (Gaza falls, annexed). The Tiglath-Pileser III page confirms the year (Gaza conquered, Ashkelon paying tribute in 734) but the Philistines page has Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron still paying tribute in 701, so no cell is removed in 734 and the whole shape is occupied (hatched); the reviewer may prefer their reading. SHAPE STEPS WITHOUT PAGES: the cuts at -1000 (north inland strip to Israel), -900 (northern coast to Israel, southern fringe to nobody) are Cliopatria's; the pages give no dates for them. AREA: no infobox area on the Philistia or Philistines pages. NO CAPITAL: Gaza is nominal. PAGE BUDGET: five pages (Philistia, Philistines, Tell es-Safi, Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy), Tiglath-Pileser III). NOT USED: Samson, Eli, the Ark (no years), Ziklag's location (uncertain), the Egyptian garrisons' withdrawal c. 1136 (Egyptian dossier). COUNTERPARTS WANTED: aram-damascus (Hazael), ashdod/ashkelon/gaza/ekron as city-states if the gap-fillers split the pentapolis. Gazetteer names wanted: Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron, Gath (Tell es-Safi), Shephelah, Sharon. FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): (1) added vassal_start/vassal_end by kingdom-of-israel (-1000..-930, confidence 1, united-monarchy page: 'client states of Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon', no year), mirroring kingdom-of-israel /ledger/2 and /9. (2) Took the Gaza district out of the founding shape and added a -1136 gain from new-kingdom-of-egypt (Ramesses VI page, confidence 2) as the reviewer's first option; new keyframe -1136 restores the full shape. DISAGREEMENT/OPEN: the Gaza circle is new-kingdom-of-egypt /ledger/22's 40 km, which also takes in Ashkelon and Ashdod, two of the Five Cities that the Philistines page puts in the first stage under Ramesses III, and the page says nothing of Gaza being Egyptian; it has Ramesses III settle them 'in strongholds, bound in my name' (Harris Papyrus), i.e. as Egyptian clients. The other 27 cells of the founding shape still lie in the Egyptian dossier's Canaan vassal region (keyframes -1200 and the -1273 vassal tint, to -1137): me-03 should either cut Philistia's cells from that region or record the Philistines as its vassal (then this dossier would add vassal_start/vassal_end by new-kingdom-of-egypt, -1150..-1136). me-03 should also change /ledger/22's counterpart from nobody to philistia. The Ramesses VI page is a sixth page (budget five). NOT DONE (thin): the capital (no page names one; Gaza nominal). FIX PASS (part 2, with the kingdom-of-israel fix): the Gibeah cell (Saul's capital, inside Philistia's Cliopatria -1150 shape) is cut from the founding shape and both keyframes, because kingdom-of-israel now holds it from -1047; Philistia's -1000 loss to Israel is restricted to the 10 cells that lie in Israel's 1000 shape (mirrored by Israel's -1000 gain from philistia) and a one-cell loss to nobody added.
